gen-fs-excon-bitter: Efficient and approachable, Excon crowds its letters together like chalk marks on a full slate, with a towering lowercase. Bitter, a slab-serif, settles into a grounded rhythm with big open eyes.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-lexend-tera: Snowburst One cuts bold, stencil-like letters with wide bridges and a tall lowercase. Lexend Tera, a sans-serif, draws a single-weight plotter-pen line with letters spaced like stepping stones, hushing the stencil's shout.
gen-audiowide-inter: Audiowide sets its tall lowercase in tile-like glyphs with wide grout lines, all one stroke thickness. Inter, a sans-serif, keeps page after page easy going, its big counters breathing like a cut reed.
gen-eater-instrument-sans: Dark and aggressive, with wide gaps between letters, Eater leads. Instrument Sans, a plain sans, goes down clean and modern, each stroke straight-edged and constant, so paragraphs stay smooth.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-lexend-mega: Loud and scattered, Paprika fills the line like capitals. Lexend Mega, a sans-serif, draws with one nib in a blueprint-like constant line, and it can sit at a modest size.
gen-irish-grover-gf-julius-sans-one: Sturdy, fun and organic: Irish Grover makes words look large. Its joins thin gently without turning spindly, while Julius Sans One, a plain sans, is best at spacing open-ended curves wide apart.
gen-righteous-gf-lexend-mega: Bowls that fill the line mark Righteous, bent like thin steel rod. Lexend Mega, a sans, keeps its one-nib strokes and open c gaps going line after line, approachable and modern.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-roboto-slab: Pramukh Rounded packs its large lowercase tight, with open bowls tipped toward you like a ladle, friendly and neutral. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif, keeps text precise and structured line to line.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-lexend-zetta: Bold, tube-like strokes mark Tilt Neon, with a splayed c. Lexend Zetta, a plain sans, spreads tall-bodied small letters wide in cut-ribbon strokes, which keeps paragraphs feeling approachable and contemporary.
gen-megrim-gf-lexend-giga: Megrim draws angular, futuristic letters with a skyward x-height line. Lexend Giga, a plain sans, runs flat, single-weight and generously tracked, so each word opens up and the text moves along smoothly.
